title: International Tax Setup grid shows every Effective Date one day early for users west of UTC (UTC-midnight date rendered in browser local time)
requirementSource: NM-4025 §4.2: 'An exact-date match must not be excluded by an off-by-one-day or timezone error.' NM-2393: grid Effective Date displays the applicable configuration version's date.
stepsToReproduce: Use a browser whose timezone is America/New_York (any US timezone).
Search Mexico / VAT / Baja California at 10/22/2026.
Read the Sales row's Effective Date.
Repeat in a browser set to Asia/Kolkata.
expectedBehavior: Sales shows 10/22/2026 in every timezone (the stored version date).
actualBehavior: New York shows 10/21/2026; Kolkata shows 10/22/2026. Every row's date is shifted back one day for users west of UTC.
networkEvidence: Search server action (POST to the page route, next-action header) returns "effectiveDate":"2026-10-22T00:00:00.000Z" for Sales; the same response renders 10/21/2026 in America/New_York. The search request itself carries the correct calendar date ("effectiveDate":"2026-10-22") and the server's as-of logic is correct (TC-TAX-IST-020..022 pass against the response).
riskNote: Users act on the displayed date: chronology for a new version must be strictly later than the latest stored date, so a user reading a date one day early can pick an invalid date or misjudge which version applies. Whether the update-section date is also shifted on Save was not observed (TC-055 payload date is correct from a UTC+9 browser).
suspectedCause: Date-only value serialised as a UTC instant and formatted with local-time date parts (e.g. new Date(iso).toLocaleDateString()). Format as a calendar date (UTC parts or a date-only string).
